sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page rapt1240 (references: Pawley & Hammarstrom 2017; Pick 2020; Z'graggen 1980; Ethnologue 2025)

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (Rapting listed as 'Lapting', Hanseman Family, 350 speakers)
sources.note: p. 6 (global remark on the transcription for all Madang District languages): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' No language-specific stress statement; typological notes on the Mabuso Stock cover only segmental phonemes and morphology.

sources.citation: Kasprus [Kaspruś], Aloys. 1942-45 [publ. 1947]. The languages of the Mugil District, NE-New Guinea. Anthropos 37-40: 711-778 (with 'Corrections', Anthropos 41-44: 370-371).
sources.note: Nothing for Ale/Rapting itself: no Ale vocabulary or sentences are given (data columns are Megiar, Matukar, Saker/Mugil, Em-Garus, Ate-Garus, with A'e-Garus in notes). The stress section (p. 734 'The basic tendency is to stress the last syllable'; p. 736 rule A 'The words are basically stressed on the last syllable', with Ate partly penultimate, pp. 736-737) is stated for those recorded languages, so it is at most an areal hint for the neighbouring Hanseman varieties, not a Rapting statement.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. hdl 10125/73354
sources.note: Not about Rapting: the language is not mentioned anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent). Its stress section (pp. ~40-41) concerns Mauwake, Pamosu and Usan (Northern Adelbert), and says stress data for most Northern Adelbert languages are 'minimal or nonexistent'. Glottolog cites it for Rapting only for subclassification.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. n.d. [uploaded 2010]. Rapting Swadesh List (6 KB). Long Now Foundation; archive.org item rosettaproject_rpt_swadesh-1 (forms identical to Z'graggen 1980 / transnewguinea.org).
sources.note: Bare wordlist, no stress or tone marks, no notes: wordlist-only data, secondhand from Z'graggen 1980.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University. (Index of languages)
sources.note: Index entry cites only Wurm & Hattori 1981 (Language Atlas of the Pacific Area) and Z'graggen 1975 - no descriptive or phonological work as of 1996.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. (Rapting = column C11)
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction sect. 6 (pp. viii-ix) says the transcription is 'semi-phonemic' and lists only segmental fluctuations for Rapting (y~z~l, d~r, s~h, k~v~w); no mention of stress anywhere in the book (a full-text search for stress/accent full text).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing; survey/village directory only. C11 Rapting, 332 speakers, villages Asiwo (140) and Lapting (192) plus (Arapik), (Bayat), (Dawali), (Solaptik); index equates Lapting = Rapting C11.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing; Rapting appears only in classification tables (pp. ~581, 601). No stress/phonology remark in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent pp. 569-612).
